_about: The Sorting Hat's yes/no questions. Each question pits two houses against each other: answering yes gives points to one house, answering no gives points to the other. Keep the house names exactly Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw or Slytherin, and give every question its own id. Try to make both answers equally easy to say out loud. If one answer sounds nicer anyway (people like to give it), mark it with "nicer": the tests check that nicer answers help and hurt every house equally, so no house quietly loses out.

questions.text: A troll is loose in the castle and a classmate is missing. Would you go looking for them yourself?
When a rule is unfair, would you rather quietly find a clever way around it than fight it openly?
Do you like to plan several steps ahead, rather than figure things out as you go?
Would you rather be remembered for one brave moment than for a lifetime of great achievements?
Is being kind more important than being clever?
Do you enjoy spending time alone with your thoughts?
Would you stay loyal to a friend, even when you think they're wrong?
Would you rather work in a team than on your own?
Would you ignore a rule that seems silly to you?
Would you rather spend an afternoon calmly repotting Mandrakes than racing around on a broomstick?
Would you rather speak your mind than keep the peace?
Do you read books that nobody told you to read?
Would you volunteer to face a dragon in the Triwizard Tournament?
The Ravenclaw common room door asks you a riddle every time you want to get in. Would you enjoy that?
Do you set yourself big goals and push hard to reach them?
Would you be happy living a quiet life, like running a little shop in Hogsmeade?
Would you like to have your face on a Chocolate Frog card one day?
Would you rather be the cleverest witch or wizard in the room than the most powerful one?
Would you rather be a brilliant inventor than a famous leader?
Do you mostly learn things because they'll be useful to you one day?
